summary: Shinten Sakai (1913–1968) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Shindo Shiraishi. He held posts at Koyasan University, where he is attested as a professor in 1970.

Shinya Moriyama (born 1972) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his master's degree at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and his doctorate at the University of Vienna (~2002–2006), later teaching at Shinshu University (~2008).

Shinya Yasutomi (1944–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and Otani University, earning a doctorate in literature in 1998. He was a professor at Otani University (~1985–2010, 2014) and directed the Institute of Shin Buddhist Studies.

Shiro Matsumoto (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Waseda University, Komazawa University, and the University of Tokyo under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He served as an assistant and professor at Komazawa University (1982, 1995–2020).

Shivram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard (~1956–1960), Shankara Shastri Marulkar, and Maheshwarshastri Joshi. He served as professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University and headed Deccan College's Sanskrit Dictionary Department.

Shizuka Sasaki (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University under Jikidō Takasaki. He served as a lecturer, associate professor, and professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University from 1990.

Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) specialized in philosophy and Indology, studying at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as a lecturer at the University of Paris (1937) and was a philosophy professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky (1900–1990) was a scholar in philosophy and history and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1918–1923) and the University of Königsberg (~1923–1924), later holding a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1928–1970).
Shobha Rani Dash works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was a researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010 and is attested as a lecturer at Otani University in 2012.
Shobhana Chelliah (born 1961) is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Texas at Austin (~1984–1990) and held a post at the University of North Texas (~1998).

Shodo Fujita (born 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami and Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

Shodo Harada (born 1940) is a Buddhist studies figure who trained at Shofukuji under Mumon Yamada (~1962–1982), whom he succeeded. He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sogenji Zen Monastery in 1995.
Shogo Watanabe (born 1953) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University (~1972–1982) and later served there as a faculty member (~1989–1999) and professor (~1999).

Shohaku Okumura (born 1948) is a Buddhist studies specialist who studied at Komazawa University (~1968–1972) and under Kosho Uchiyama (1970–1975). He founded Sanshin Zen Community and served as director of the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997–2010).

Shoji Mori (born 1938) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University (~1962–1971) under Giyu Nishi, worked at the Okura Institute for the Study of Spiritual Culture (~1971–1977), and was an associate professor and professor at Toyo University (~1977–2009).
Shoju Inaba (1915–1990) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Otani University (~1958–1980) and served as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.
Shojun Bando (1932–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1956). He held posts at Otani University and Ueno Gakuen University.

Shokin Furuta (1911–2001) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Education under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He was a professor at Hokkaido University (~1960–1974) and Nihon University (~1974–1981), and directed Matsugaoka Bunko.
Shoko Kanaoka (1930–2004) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 1987 and 2000).

Shoko Miyabayashi (1932–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his undergraduate and master's degrees at Taisho University (1948–1955), where he later served as lecturer, associate professor, and Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).
